what_happened: The job to give OLY-8-05 (the critic's adversarial challenge) a mechanism was rejected at the final verdict. One of 4 acceptance criteria was unmet: the one requiring cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets and cargo test to all pass. There was one major finding and no blockers: behavior criterion 3 is unmet because its evidence must cite commands that ran (D43). One check failed: the test check. Shard 3 of 6 reported that 1 of 11 units failed, athena-cli --test drain. The kept output shows only the passing doc-test lines of another shard, so the failing test name and assertion are not visible.
cause: The test check ended the job, and the output kept for it does not show what failed. It holds the tail of the passing athena-score doc-test shard plus the runner's exit line, so the drain test failure cannot be diagnosed from the record. Nothing extracts the failing test name and assertion into the kept evidence. Separately, the criterion's behavior evidence (D43) was not tied to commands the producer ran. As a result the verifier rejected the job on the failed test check and on missing command evidence, and neither could be judged against what the job changed.
other_causes: The producer was likely not required to cite the commands it ran as evidence for the behavior criterion, so D43 was met only at the final verdict.
The athena-cli drain test may be affected by the job's change to critic or drain behavior, or may be an unrelated or flaky failure; no baseline is recorded to tell which.
open_hypotheses: Whether the athena-cli --test drain failure was caused by this job's changes or was pre-existing or flaky.
Whether the producer ran cargo test locally and saw the drain failure before finishing.
Whether the critic prompt change affected a budget or doc figure, as in the earlier case 20261110-180450-460g; the fields do not show this.
contradictions: The earlier case 20261110-180450-460g was rejected for a failing budgets test, but this failure is in the drain test, so the cause may differ even though the D43 finding is the same.
The class description says the kept output is only CI cleanup and warnings. Here the output at least names the failing unit (athena-cli --test drain), so the failure is partly visible.
prevention: When a test check fails, the kept evidence must include the failing test name and its assertion output, taken from the failed shard and not the tail of the log. A code check should refuse to record a failed test check whose kept output has no 'FAILED' or 'panicked' line. Also, the producer brief should require citing the commands it ran for behavior criteria (D43), and running the full cargo test before finishing. Either would have exposed the drain failure and the evidence gap before the final verdict.

First run cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain on the base and on your change, and report which tests fail and why. If it fails on the base too, say so and do not fix it unless it blocks this job. Make sure cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings and cargo test all pass. For each behavior criterion, cite the exact commands you ran and their results as evidence (D43). Update any budget figure in docs/system-facts.md if the critic prompt size changes, and add the CHANGELOG.md entry.
